title: Mixed Phase Iron Oxides Thin Layers by CVD Method
author: Parra-Elizondo, Cuentas-Gallegos, et al.
materials: The following steps occur sequentially and comprehend the experimental APCVD system:(a)The addition of the precursor (100 mg) into the modified round heating baker. Connection of the line for the carrier gas from the volumetric gas controller to the modified round precursor heating gas port. Assure sealing between fittings in the pair feeding glass fixture.(b)Undertake the connection of the O3 generator outlet gas tube to the feeding glass manifold such that it accommodates the second gas inlet in the feeding glass fixture.(c)Place the deposition 316 L substrate over the refractory cement holder, positioned within the quartz tube at the half of tube length.(d)Securely fasten both the feeding glass fittings and the end glass fittings on opposite sides of the quartz tube and establish a gas exhaust connection to the water trap at the quartz tube's terminal end.(e)Undertake the system's purge by employing a constant flow of N2 at 60 sccm for 10 min. This procedure also aims to verify the efficacy of the sealing intersections and identify any potential gas leaks within the synthesis system.(f)Direct the heating element for precursor vaporization to 160 °C to sublime the organometallic precursor.(g)Undertake the initiation of the tubular furnace heating program with a temperature increase at a rate of 10 °C per minute, until the designated experimental temperature of 330 °C, 430 °C, or 530 °C is maintained, subsequently holding the temperature for 60 min.(h)Monitor the temperature of the heating element for the organometallic precursor with a thermometer. When the temperature has reached 160 °C, activate the N2 displacement gas at a flow rate of 60 sccm to initiate the deposition process.(i)Initiate the O3 generator and stabilize the outlet flow rate at 60 sccm for an hour.(j)Upon the reaction time is completed (60 min), shut down the O3 generator and carefully remove the quartz tube from the system when the temperature of the system is at room level.(k)Extract the as-deposited substrates for characterization.

steps.title: Load precursor and connect carrier gas
steps.instruction: Place 100 mg of the organometallic precursor into the modified round heating baker and connect the carrier‑gas line from the volumetric gas controller to the precursor heating gas port, ensuring a sealed fit between the pair of feeding‑glass fittings.

steps.title: Connect ozone generator line
steps.instruction: Attach the O₃ generator outlet tube to the feeding‑glass manifold so that it aligns with the second gas inlet in the feeding‑glass fixture, confirming a secure seal.

steps.title: Install substrate in quartz tube
steps.instruction: Place the 316 L deposition substrate onto the refractory cement holder and position it at the midpoint of the quartz tube.

steps.title: Seal tube and attach exhaust
steps.instruction: Tightly fasten the feeding‑glass fittings on one side and the end‑glass fittings on the opposite side of the quartz tube, then connect the gas‑exhaust line to a water trap located at the terminal end of the quartz tube.

steps.title: Purge system with nitrogen
steps.instruction: Purge the entire assembly with a constant flow of N₂ at 60 sccm for 10 min to verify sealing integrity and detect any leaks.

steps.title: Heat precursor to vaporize
steps.instruction: Set the heating element for the precursor to 160 °C to sublime the organometallic precursor.

steps.title: Ramp furnace to target temperature
steps.instruction: Program the tubular furnace to increase temperature at 10 °C min⁻¹ until reaching the chosen experimental temperature (330 °C, 430 °C, or 530 °C) and then hold that temperature for 60 min.

steps.title: Start nitrogen flow for deposition
steps.instruction: When the precursor heating element reaches 160 °C, activate the N₂ displacement gas at 60 sccm to begin the deposition process.

steps.title: Introduce ozone flow
steps.instruction: Turn on the O₃ generator and stabilize its outlet flow at 60 sccm, maintaining this flow for 1 hour (the 60‑min deposition period).

steps.title: Terminate reaction and cool
steps.instruction: After the 60‑min reaction, shut down the O₃ generator, allow the system to cool to room temperature, and then carefully remove the quartz tube from the apparatus.

steps.title: Collect deposited substrates
steps.instruction: Extract the as‑deposited substrates from the holder for subsequent characterization.
